{{Nihongo|'''Kurume Suitengū'''|久留米水天宮|}} is a [[Shinto]] {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|qid=Q320934|lt=Kurume}}, [[Fukuoka prefecture]], [[Japan]]. This shrine is the headquarters for all Suitengū Shrines in Japan.
It is dedicated to four deities:
* [[Ame-no-Minakanushi|Amenominakanushi]]
* [[Emperor Antoku|Antoku]]
* [[Taira no Tokuko|Kenrenmon-in]]
* {{ill|Taira no Tokiko|en|Taira no Tokiko|qid=Q3379244|lt=Nii No Ama}}
"Suiten" is the [[Japan|Japanese]] name of the deity of [[Hindu]] origins {{ill|Varuna|en|Varuna|qid=Q1001037|lt=Varuna}}, one of a series of Hindu deities whose worship entered Japan together with [[Buddhism]].. When the Japanese Empire enforced the ''[[Shinbutsu bunri]]'', the official separation of Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples, shrines celebrating Suiten identified their dedication to [[Amenominakanushi]].
==Legends==
As a shrine related with {{ill|Water|en|Water|qid=Q283|lt=Water}}, Suitengū came to be venerated as a guardian shrine for [[:en:Ship transport|marine traffic]] and was said to have a connection with the legend of [[Kappa (folklore)|Kappa]]. These days, it is believed to house the [[Kami|god]] of safe childbirth.
